p.src: Meanwhile, Kongming rode out in his small carriage with several hundred horsemen to reconnoiter the road ahead. Before them lay a river called the Western Er River. Though its current was gentle, not a single boat or raft could be found. Kongming ordered trees felled and made into rafts for the crossing, but every piece of timber sank when put into the water. Kongming therefore questioned Lü Kai, who replied, “I have heard that upstream on the Western Er River stands a mountain thick with bamboo, some stalks several arm-spans around. Men could be sent to cut it down and build a bamboo bridge over the river for the army and horses to cross.” Kongming at once sent thirty thousand men into the mountain. They cut several hundred thousand bamboo poles and floated them downstream, then built a bamboo bridge more than ten zhang wide at a narrow point in the river. He then deployed the main army in a single line of camps on the north bank, using the river as a moat, the floating bridge as a gate, and banks of earth as walls; and across the bridge on the south bank he established three great camps in a line to await the southern troops.

p.src: Meanwhile, Meng Huo came on in fury at the head of several hundred thousand southern troops. As he neared the Western Er River, Meng Huo led a vanguard of ten thousand shield-and-sword warriors straight to the forward camp and challenged its defenders. Kongming emerged in a four-horse carriage, wearing a silk cap and crane-feather cloak and holding his feather fan, with his generals clustered around him. Kongming saw Meng Huo clad in rhinoceros-hide armor and a vermilion helmet, a shield on his left arm and a sword in his right hand, riding a red-haired ox and shouting abuse; while more than ten thousand tribal warriors under him brandished swords and shields, charging to and fro. Kongming hastily ordered a withdrawal into the main camp, had it tightly closed on every side, and forbade anyone to give battle. The southern soldiers, naked to the waist, came right up to the camp gate and shouted insults. The generals were enraged and all reported to Kongming, “We are willing to leave the camp and fight them to the death!” Kongming refused permission. Again and again the generals asked to fight, but Kongming merely checked them, saying, “The people of those southern regions do not submit to the civilizing rule of the court. They have arrived now at the height of their savage fury and must not be met head-on. We should hold firm for several days. When their arrogance has somewhat slackened, I shall have a subtle plan to defeat them.”

p.src: And so the Shu troops held their ground for several days. Kongming observed from high ground and, seeing that the southern soldiers had grown lax, assembled his generals and asked, “Do you dare go out and fight?” The generals eagerly volunteered to go. Kongming first summoned Zhao Yun and Wei Yan into his tent, whispered in their ears, and instructed them in every detail of his plan. The two received their orders and went on ahead. He next summoned Wang Ping and Ma Zhong into the tent; they too received their instructions and departed. Then he summoned Ma Dai and instructed him, “I shall now abandon these three camps and retreat across the river to its north bank. Once our army has withdrawn, dismantle the floating bridge, move it downstream, and use it to bring Zhao Yun’s and Wei Yan’s troops back across the river to reinforce us.” Ma Dai received the plan and departed. Then Kongming summoned Zhang Yi and said, “When our army withdraws, leave many lamps burning in the camps. When Meng Huo learns of our retreat, he will certainly pursue us; you are to cut off his rear.” Zhang Yi received his orders and withdrew. Kongming ordered only Guan Suo to guard his carriage. The troops withdrew, leaving many lights burning throughout the camps. Seeing them, the southern soldiers did not dare make an assault.

p.src: At dawn the next day, Meng Huo led the main body straight to the Shu camps. He found all three great camps deserted, with several hundred wagons of provisions and equipment abandoned inside. Meng You said, “Zhuge Liang has abandoned his camps and fled. Could this be some stratagem?” Meng Huo replied, “I judge that Zhuge Liang has abandoned his baggage and gone because some urgent crisis has arisen in his country. If Wu has not invaded, then Wei must have attacked. That is why he made a great display of lights to deceive us and then abandoned his wagons and equipment. We must pursue him quickly and not let this chance slip by.” Meng Huo therefore drove his vanguard onward to the bank of the Western Er River. Looking across to the north bank, he saw the banners in the camp as orderly as ever, gleaming like embroidered clouds; and all along the river stood further lines of splendidly adorned defenses. The southern scouts saw this and none dared advance. Meng Huo said to Meng You, “Zhuge Liang fears our pursuit and has therefore halted briefly on the north bank. Within two days he is certain to flee.” He then encamped his southern troops along the riverbank; and sent men up the mountain to cut bamboo and make rafts in readiness for crossing the river; while all his best fighting men were moved to the front of the camp. He did not know that the Shu troops had long since entered his own territory.

p.src: That day, a violent wind arose. Fire blazed and war drums thundered on every side as the Shu troops charged in. The southern warriors collided with one another in confusion. Meng Huo was greatly alarmed and hurriedly led his clansmen and tribal troops in cutting a path through the enemy, making straight for the old camps. Suddenly, a fierce body of troops charged out from the camp—it was Zhao Yun. Meng Huo turned back in panic toward the Western Er River and fled into the remote mountains. Another fierce body of troops came charging out—it was Ma Dai. Left with only a few dozen beaten and exhausted soldiers, Meng Huo fled toward a mountain valley. Seeing clouds of dust and flames to the south, north, and west, he dared not advance in any of those directions and had no choice but to flee eastward. He had just rounded a mountain pass when he saw several dozen attendants before a great wood escorting a small carriage; seated upright in the carriage was Kongming, who laughed heartily and cried, “King Meng Huo of the South! Heaven has brought you to defeat here, and I have been waiting for you a long time!” Meng Huo was enraged and looked back at his men, saying, “I have fallen victim to this man’s treacherous schemes! Three times have I suffered humiliation; but now, by good fortune, I have met him here. Charge with all your strength and hack both man and carriage to pieces!” Several southern horsemen spurred fiercely forward. Meng Huo shouted in the lead and charged up to the great wood. With a sudden crash, they triggered a pitfall and all tumbled in together. Wei Yan emerged from the wood with several hundred soldiers, who dragged the captives out one by one and bound them securely with ropes. Kongming returned to the camp first and offered amnesty to the southern soldiers, the district chieftains, and their tribal warriors. By then, more than half had already returned to their native villages. Apart from the dead and wounded, all the rest surrendered. Kongming treated them to wine and meat, soothed them with kind words, and ordered that every one of them be released. The southern soldiers departed, deeply moved and sighing with gratitude.

p.src: Before long, Zhang Yi arrived escorting the captive Meng You. Kongming admonished him, saying, “Your elder brother is foolish and deluded; you ought to remonstrate with him. Now that I have captured him four times, how can he have the face to appear before others again?” Meng You’s face filled with shame. He prostrated himself and begged to be spared. Kongming said, “Today is not the day I shall kill you. For now I shall spare your life. Go and counsel your brother.” He ordered the guards to untie the ropes and help Meng You to his feet. Meng You wept, bowed, and departed. Soon afterward, Wei Yan arrived escorting the captive Meng Huo. Kongming cried angrily, “Now you have been captured by me yet again. What defense can you possibly offer?” Meng Huo said, “This time I blundered into a treacherous scheme. I could not close my eyes in death!” Kongming barked at the guards to take him out and behead him. Meng Huo showed not the slightest fear. Looking back at Kongming, he said, “If you dare release me once more, I shall certainly avenge the humiliation of these four captures!” Kongming laughed heartily, ordered his attendants to remove Meng Huo’s bonds, gave him wine to settle his nerves, and seated him in the tent. Kongming asked, “I have now treated you with courtesy four times, yet you still refuse to submit. Why?” Meng Huo replied, “Though I am a man beyond the reach of civilized rule, I do not, like you, Prime Minister, rely solely upon treacherous schemes. How could I willingly submit?” Kongming said, “If I release you once more, can you still fight?” Meng Huo replied, “If the Prime Minister captures me yet again, then I shall submit with all my heart, offer everything in my own domain to reward your army, and swear never to rebel again.”

p.src: Kongming smiled and sent him on his way. Meng Huo gladly bowed his thanks and departed. He then gathered several thousand able-bodied men from the various caves and made his way steadily southward. Before long he saw dust rising in the distance as a troop approached. It was his brother Meng You, who had rallied the surviving troops and come to avenge him. The brothers embraced and wept, then recounted all that had happened. Meng You said, “Our forces have suffered defeat after defeat, while the Shu army has won time and again. We cannot withstand them. Our only course is to withdraw into a cave on the shaded side of the mountains and refuse to come out. The Shu troops will be unable to endure the heat and will retreat of their own accord.” Meng Huo asked, “Where can we take refuge?” Meng You replied, “Southwest of here lies a cave called Bald Dragon Cave. Its lord, King Duosi, is a close friend of mine. We may seek shelter with him.”

p.src: Meng Huo therefore sent Meng You ahead to Bald Dragon Cave to meet King Duosi. Duosi hastily led the cave troops out to welcome them. Meng Huo entered the cave, exchanged courtesies, and related all that had happened. Duosi said, “Set your mind at ease, my king. If the Shu army comes, not one man or horse shall return home; they and Zhuge Liang will all perish here!” Meng Huo was overjoyed and asked Duosi what plan he had. Duosi said, “There are only two roads through this cave. One approaches from the northeast—the road by which Your Majesty came. The terrain is level, the soil deep, and the water sweet, so men and horses can pass. If we barricade the cave entrance with timber and stones, even an army of a million will be unable to advance. Another road comes from the northwest, where the mountains are perilous, the ridges forbidding, and the way narrow. Though narrow paths run through it, venomous snakes and vicious scorpions lurk everywhere. At dusk, poisonous miasma rises and does not clear until the hours of the Snake and Horse; passage is possible only during the hours of the Goat, Monkey, and Rooster. The water cannot be drunk, and neither men nor horses can travel easily. Moreover, there are four poisonous springs here. The first is called the Mute Spring. Its water is quite sweet, but anyone who drinks it loses the power of speech and invariably dies within ten days. The second is called the Destroying Spring. Its water is no different from boiling broth; anyone who bathes in it has his skin and flesh rot away and dies once the bones are exposed. The third is called the Black Spring. Its water looks somewhat clear, but anyone splashed by it turns black in the hands and feet and dies. The fourth is called the Soft Spring. Its water is cold as ice; anyone who drinks it loses all warmth in the throat, grows limp as cotton, and dies. Neither insects nor birds live in this region; only General Fubo of the Han ever reached it. Since his time, not a single person has come here. We shall now barricade the great northeastern road and let Your Majesty dwell securely in my humble cave. When the Shu troops find the eastern road blocked, they will surely enter by the western route. There is no water along that road. When they see these four springs, they will certainly drink from them; even an army of a million will have none return alive. What need have we of weapons?” Meng Huo was delighted. Raising a hand to his brow, he exclaimed, “Only today have I found a place of refuge!” Then, pointing northward, he said, “However wondrous Zhuge Liang’s calculations and stratagems, he will find no way to employ them here! The waters of the four springs will be enough to avenge the humiliation of my defeated army!” From then on, Meng Huo and Meng You feasted all day with King Duosi.

p.src: As Kongming led the great army onward, a scout suddenly galloped up and reported, “Meng Huo has retreated into Bald Dragon Cave and refuses to come out. He has barricaded the vital road at the cave entrance and stationed troops within to guard it. The mountains are rugged and the ridges steep, so we cannot advance.” Kongming summoned Lü Kai and questioned him. Lü Kai replied, “I have heard that there is a road through this cave, but I do not know the details.” Jiang Wan said, “Meng Huo has been captured four times and has already lost his courage. How would he dare come out again? Moreover, the weather is now scorching, and our men and horses are exhausted. There is no profit in continuing the campaign. It would be better to withdraw the army and return home.” Kongming replied, “If we do that, we will fall directly into Meng Huo’s scheme. The moment our army retreats, he will surely take advantage of the situation and pursue us. Now that we have come this far, how can there be any reason to turn back?” He therefore ordered Wang Ping to lead several hundred soldiers as the vanguard. He had the newly surrendered southern troops guide them along a narrow path to the northwest. They came to a spring. Men and horses alike were thirsty and rushed to drink its water. Having reconnoitered the route, Wang Ping returned to report to Kongming. By the time they reached the main camp, none of them could speak; they could only point at their mouths.

p.src: Kongming was greatly alarmed and knew they had been poisoned. He therefore rode out in his small carriage with several dozen men to investigate. They found a pool of clear water, so deep that its bottom could not be seen and exuding an icy vapor. None of the soldiers dared taste it. Kongming alighted, climbed to high ground, and surveyed the place. Peaks and ridges enclosed it on every side, and not a bird could be heard. He grew deeply suspicious. Suddenly, he caught sight of an ancient temple on a distant ridge. Kongming climbed up by grasping vines and creepers. Inside a stone chamber he found the image of a general seated upright, with a stone tablet beside it. This was the temple of Ma Yuan, General Fubo of the Han. When he had come here to pacify the southern tribes, the local people had built the temple to worship him. Kongming bowed twice and prayed, “I, Liang, received from the late Emperor the weighty charge of caring for his orphaned heir, and now, in obedience to the imperial command, I have come here to pacify the southern tribes. Once the southern lands are pacified, I intend to conquer Wei, annex Wu, and restore peace to the house of Han. Now my soldiers, ignorant of the terrain, have mistakenly drunk poisonous water and can no longer utter a sound. I earnestly beseech your honored spirit to remember the grace and loyalty owed to our dynasty, manifest your divine power, and protect the whole army!”

p.src: When he had finished praying, he left the temple to seek a local inhabitant and ask about the water. In the distance, on the opposite mountain, he faintly saw an old man approaching with a staff, strikingly unusual in appearance. Kongming invited the old man into the temple. After exchanging courtesies, they sat facing one another on the stones. Kongming asked, “May I know your honored name, venerable sir?” The old man replied, “I have long heard of the illustrious fame of the great kingdom’s chancellor, and count myself fortunate to meet you. Many people of the southern lands owe their lives to Your Excellency, and all are deeply grateful.” Kongming asked about the spring, and the old man replied, “The water your soldiers drank came from the Mute Spring. Those who drink it lose the power of speech and die within a few days. Besides this spring, there are three others. To the southeast is a spring whose water is bitterly cold. Anyone who drinks it loses all warmth in the throat, grows limp and weak, and dies. It is called the Soft Spring. Due south is a spring whose water turns the hands and feet black and kills anyone splashed by it. It is called the Black Spring. To the southwest is a spring that boils like hot broth. Anyone who bathes in it has all his skin and flesh slough away and dies. It is called the Destroying Spring. These four springs lie in our region, where poisonous vapors gather. No medicine can cure their effects. The miasma also rises densely, and passage is possible only during the three hours of the Goat, Monkey, and Rooster. At all other hours the miasma lies thick, and anyone who touches it dies at once.”

Kongming invited the old man into the temple. After exchanging courtesies, they sat facing one another on the stones.
Kongming asked, “May I know your honored name, venerable sir?”

p.src: Kongming said, “If that is so, the southern lands can never be pacified. And if the south remains unpacified, how can I annex Wu and Wei and restore the house of Han? I would have failed the late Emperor’s weighty charge to me as guardian of his heir; death would be better than life!” The old man said, “Prime Minister, do not be troubled. I shall direct you to a place where this difficulty may be remedied.” Kongming said, “What wise counsel have you, venerable sir? I beg you to instruct me.” The old man said, “Several li due west of here lies a mountain valley. Twenty li within it flows a stream called the Stream of Ten Thousand Blessings. There dwells a worthy recluse known as the Hermit of Ten Thousand Blessings; he has not left that stream for more than several decades. Behind his thatched hermitage is a spring called the Spring of Peace and Joy. If anyone is poisoned, drawing and drinking its water will cure him at once. Those afflicted with scabies or infected by miasma need only bathe in the Stream of Ten Thousand Blessings to recover naturally. Moreover, before the hermitage grows a kind of herb called ‘chive-leaf rue.’ If a person holds one leaf in his mouth, the miasma cannot infect him. You should hasten there and ask him for aid.” Kongming bowed in thanks and asked, “I can never sufficiently express my gratitude for your life-saving kindness. May I learn your honored name?” The old man entered the temple and said, “I am the local mountain god. At the command of General Fubo, I came expressly to guide you.” With that, he shouted, split open the stone wall behind the temple, and entered it. Kongming was filled with amazement. He bowed twice more before the temple god, retraced his former path, mounted his carriage, and returned to the main camp.

p.src: The next day, Kongming prepared fine incense and gifts, then took Wang Ping and all the mute soldiers and traveled through the night toward the place named by the mountain god, proceeding gradually onward. They entered a narrow mountain path and traveled some twenty li, where they saw tall pines, great cypresses, luxuriant bamboo, and wondrous flowers encircling a hamlet; within the fences stood several thatched cottages, and a fragrant scent filled their nostrils. Kongming was delighted. He reached the hamlet and knocked at a door, whereupon a young boy came out. Just as Kongming was about to give his name, a man appeared, wearing a bamboo cap and straw sandals, a white robe bound with a black sash. He had blue eyes and yellow hair, and came out cheerfully, saying, “Can the visitor be none other than the Prime Minister of Han?” Kongming smiled and said, “How did you know, worthy sir?” The hermit replied, “I have long heard that the Prime Minister’s great standard was advancing south. How could I not know?” He then invited Kongming into the thatched hall. After exchanging courtesies, host and guest took their appointed seats. Kongming told him, “I, Liang, received from Emperor Zhaolie the weighty charge of safeguarding his orphaned heir. Now, by the sacred command of the reigning sovereign, I have led a great army here to subdue the southern tribes and bring them under the transforming influence of the royal realm. Unexpectedly, Meng Huo slipped away into the caves, while my soldiers mistakenly drank from the Mute Spring. Last night General Fubo manifested his divine presence and told me that you possessed a medicinal spring able to cure them. I beg you to take pity and grant us the divine water, that the wretched lives of these soldiers may be saved.” The hermit said, “I am merely a useless old rustic. Why trouble the Prime Minister to honor me with a visit? The spring lies just behind the hermitage.” He ordered water to be fetched for them to drink.

p.src: Thereupon the boy led Wang Ping and the company of mute soldiers to the stream, where they drew water and drank; at once they spat out foul saliva and regained their speech. The boy then led all the soldiers to bathe in the Stream of Ten Thousand Blessings. In the hermitage, the recluse served Kongming tea made from cypress seeds and a dish of pine pollen. The hermit told him, “The tribal caves here abound in venomous snakes and vicious scorpions. Willow blossoms drift into the streams and springs, so their water must not be drunk; only water from a spring dug into the earth is safe to draw and drink.” Kongming asked for the ‘chive-leaf rue,’ and the hermit let the soldiers gather as much as they wished, saying, “Let each man hold one leaf in his mouth, and the miasma will naturally be unable to invade him.” Kongming bowed and asked the hermit’s name. The hermit laughed and said, “I am Meng Jie, elder brother of Meng Huo.” Kongming was astonished. The hermit continued, “Prime Minister, harbor no doubts, but allow me a few words of explanation. My parents had three sons: I, Meng Jie, am the eldest; Meng Huo is the second, and Meng You the youngest. Our parents are both dead. My two younger brothers are violent and wicked and refuse to submit to the royal civilizing order. I admonished them repeatedly, but they would not listen; therefore I changed both my given name and surname and came to live here in seclusion. Now I am shamed by my brothers’ rebellion, which has also forced the Prime Minister to penetrate this barren wilderness and endure such hardship. I, Meng Jie, deserve ten thousand deaths, and therefore beg forgiveness before you.” Kongming sighed and said, “Only now do I truly believe that the tale of Robber Zhi and Liuxia Hui can also occur in our own age.” Then he said to Meng Jie, “Shall I memorialize the Son of Heaven and have you established as king?” Meng Jie replied, “I fled here precisely because I wished to avoid fame and achievement. How could I still harbor any desire for wealth and rank?” Kongming then presented him with gold and silk. Meng Jie firmly refused to accept them. Kongming sighed in admiration without cease, then bowed farewell and returned. A later poet wrote:

p.src: When Kongming returned to the main camp, he ordered the soldiers to dig into the earth for water. They dug more than twenty zhang deep, yet found not a single drop; they dug at more than ten places, and every one was the same. Alarm spread through the army. At midnight Kongming burned incense and appealed to Heaven: “I, your servant Liang, am without talent, yet by the blessing of the great Han I received the command to pacify the south. Now we lack water on the road, and men and horses are parched with thirst. If Heaven has not abandoned the great Han, then grant us sweet springs! But if its ordained fortune is already at an end, then I, Liang, and all the rest are willing to die here!” When his prayer was finished that night, they looked at dawn and found every well brimming with sweet water. p.src: Once Kongming’s men and horses had obtained sweet water, they proceeded safely along the narrow path and encamped directly before Bald Dragon Cave. Tribal scouts learned of this and reported to Meng Huo: “The Shu troops have not been infected by the miasmic pestilence, nor do they suffer from thirst. None of the springs has had any effect.” King Duosi heard the report but would not believe it, so he and Meng Huo climbed a high mountain to observe. They saw the Shu soldiers entirely unharmed, carrying water and drink in great barrels and small shoulder loads, watering their horses and cooking their meals. At the sight, Duosi’s hair stood on end. He turned to Meng Huo and said, “These are divine troops!” Meng Huo said, “My brother and I shall fight the Shu army to the death. Even if we fall before their ranks, how could we submit tamely to be bound?” Duosi said, “If Your Majesty’s army is defeated, my wife and children will be finished as well. We must slaughter oxen and horses, reward the cave warriors lavishly, and charge straight into the Shu camp without shrinking from flood or flame. Only then can we prevail.”

p.src: Accordingly, they bestowed rich rewards on the tribal troops. Just as they were about to set out, a sudden report came that Yang Feng, lord of the twenty-one caves of Silver Mine Cave west beyond the rear of their own cave, was leading thirty thousand troops to aid them in battle. Meng Huo was overjoyed and said, “Our neighboring forces have come to aid me. Victory is surely mine!” He and King Duosi at once went out of the cave to welcome them. Yang Feng led his troops inside and said, “I have thirty thousand elite soldiers, all clad in iron armor. They can fly over mountains and cross ridges, and are enough to withstand a million soldiers of Shu; I also have five sons, each thoroughly trained in the martial arts. We wish to aid Your Majesty.” Yang Feng ordered his five sons to enter and bow. All were powerful and tiger-built, brimming with martial grandeur. Meng Huo was delighted and arranged a banquet for Yang Feng and his sons. When they were half-drunk, Yang Feng said, “There is little entertainment in the army. Among my followers are tribal maidens skilled at dancing with swords and shields. Let them provide us with some amusement.” Meng Huo gladly agreed. Presently, several dozen tribal maidens, all with loose hair and bare feet, danced and leapt into the tent from outside, while the assembled tribesmen clapped their hands and sang in accompaniment. Yang Feng ordered two of his sons to offer wine. The two sons raised their cups and approached Meng Huo and Meng You. The two men accepted the cups and were just about to drink when Yang Feng gave a mighty shout. His sons instantly seized Meng Huo and Meng You and dragged them from their seats. King Duosi was about to flee, but Yang Feng had already captured him. The tribal maidens barred the way across the tent, and none dared come forward. Meng Huo said, “When the rabbit dies, the fox grieves; creatures mourn for their own kind. You and I are both lords of our respective caves, and there has never been enmity between us. Why do you seek to harm me?” Yang Feng replied, “My brothers, sons, and nephews have all received the life-saving grace of Prime Minister Zhuge, and we had no means to repay him. Now that you have rebelled, why should I not seize you and present you to him?”

Kongming ordered them brought in. Yang Feng and the others bowed before his command tent and said, “Our sons and nephews are all grateful for the Prime Minister’s benevolence. We have therefore captured Meng Huo, Meng You, and the others and brought them here to present to you.” Kongming rewarded them handsomely and ordered Meng Huo driven before him. Kongming laughed and said, “Will you submit wholeheartedly this time?” Meng Huo replied, “This was not due to your ability. It was my own tribesmen who turned upon one another and brought me to this pass. Kill me if you wish—I still will not submit!” Kongming said, “You lured me into a waterless region and then assailed us with the deadly Dumb Spring, Spring of Destruction, Black Spring, and Soft Spring, yet my army came to no harm. Was this not the will of Heaven? Why do you remain so obstinately deluded?” Meng Huo said again, “My ancestral home lies in the Silver Pit Mountains, protected by the natural barriers of the Three Rivers and by strong, successive passes. If you capture me there, then my children and all their descendants shall serve you with wholehearted devotion.” Kongming said, “I shall release you once more. Go back, marshal your forces anew, and settle victory or defeat with me. But if I capture you then and you still refuse to submit, I shall exterminate your nine kindreds.” He sharply ordered his attendants to remove the bonds and set Meng Huo free.
